newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN DOLLAR CLOSES LOWER IN NARROW-RANGE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN DOLLAR CLOSES LOWER IN NARROW-RANGE TRADE.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar finished lower against its U.S. counterpart on Wednesday, but dealers saw limited downside for the local unit due to the central bank's strong defence.
The local unit struggled to circle in a narrow T$28.721-727 range throughout Wednesday's session. It ended at T$28.727 against Tuesday's T$28.718 close.
Turnover through dealers was active at US$228.5 million.
"The central bank defended the Taiwan dollar at T$28.727 level right from the beginning," said one dealer.
"Knowing the central bank's bottomline, there is no point of fighting with the bank," the dealer at a foreign bank said.
"You can say we give up the battle without even fighting it," he said.
Dealers said the U.S. dollar's strength overseas continued to trigger greenback buying, especially from local importers, but the local unit's fall would be limited.
They said they expected some outflow of foreign equity funds on Thursday following the stock market's Wednesday plunge.
The Taiwan share prices fell 2.57 percent on Wednesday, reflecting overnight losses in Wall Street and Nasdaq.
A range of T$28.65-75 was seen for Thursday.
